card.summary: H.R. 5371, the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, ends the government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. It provides temporary funding for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, full-year funding for specific sectors like agriculture, military construction, and veterans affairs, and extends various expiring federal programs, authorities, and health care flexibilities.

card.summary: H.R. 3944 provides fiscal year 2026 appropriations for federal programs and activities relating to military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, agriculture, rural development, the Food and Drug Administration, and the legislative branch. The legislation comprises three regular appropriations acts: the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026; the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026; and the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026.

card.label: S. 2257

latest_action.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 113.

card.summary: S. 2257, the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026, provides federal funding and sets financial rules for operations within the legislative branch of the U.S. government for fiscal year 2026. The bill covers funding for the Senate, joint congressional committees, the Capitol Police, the Congressional Budget Office, the Architect of the Capitol, the Library of Congress, the Government Publishing Office, and the Government Accountability Office, while excluding House-specific funding.
card.title: Legislative Branch Appropriations Act, 2026

summary: H.R. 4249 provides fiscal year 2026 appropriations and sets rules for operations, programs, and agencies of the legislative branch of the U.S. government, excluding the Senate.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to funding levels, intern allowances, vehicle lease limits, and rules regarding office expenditures and prohibited technologies.
affected_groups.group: Members of Congress and House Staff

affected_groups.effect: Receive specific appropriations for salaries and general expenses, with funds restricted from certain foreign drone purchases and new training rules.
Subject to bans on supplying certain foreign-linked information technology, telecommunications equipment, and vehicles, and restrictions on incentive payments if behind schedule.

key_provisions: Appropriates funds for the House of Representatives, joint items, Capitol Police, Congressional Budget Office, Architect of the Capitol, Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, and Government Accountability Office.
Mandates that any unused funds from Members' Representational Allowances be deposited in the Treasury for deficit or debt reduction.
Prohibits the use of funds to procure certain information technology, telecommunications equipment, or vehicles linked to China or specified restricted entities.
Blocks the use of funds for diversity, equity, and inclusion training or implementation that promotes divisive concepts related to race or sex.
Prohibits the federal government from taking discriminatory action against persons acting on sincerely held religious beliefs or moral convictions that marriage is between one man and one woman.
Denies any cost-of-living salary adjustments for Members of Congress during fiscal year 2026.
Permits the payment of compensation to officers or employees under the DACA program regardless of traditional immigration status if they hold an employment authorization document.
